主要内容: Experts predict it will take at least a decade before consumers can purchase self-driving cars, according to a J.D. Power survey. The survey highlights that challenges in perfecting self-driving technology will delay the widespread adoption of autonomous vehicles. Industry insiders estimate that robotaxis will not be ready for public use until 2025, and fully autonomous vehicles will not be available for private buyers until at least 2034. Meanwhile, consumers expect self-driving vehicles to be ready for various uses in the near future. The survey also notes that regulatory hurdles and the need for technological perfection are major obstacles to the development of self-driving cars. Companies like General Motors and Tesla are adjusting their timelines for launching autonomous services, with Cruise postponing its ride-share service and Tesla CEO Elon Musk maintaining his forecast for 1 million self-driving Teslas by the end of next year. Experts suggest that it will take at least a decade before self-driving cars become widely available. The slow acceptance of electric vehicles (EVs) is attributed to consumer reluctance to switch from gas-powered models. According to Kolodge, while consumers recognize the environmental benefits of EVs, they remain hesitant to adopt battery electric vehicles. This resistance highlights the challenges in transitioning to sustainable transportation. Additionally, J.D. Power collaborated with SurveyMonkey to conduct a survey of over 100 auto and tech experts for its first Mobility Confidence Index, emphasizing the need for greater consumer confidence in EVs and autonomous technologies.
